paper.title: SIMD-oriented Fast Mersenne Twister: a 128-bit Pseudorandom Number Generator
paper.venue: Monte Carlo and Quasi-Monte Carlo Methods 2006 (Springer)

program.how: written for ounce-core as plain integer C from the paper's recurrence on 128-bit words (N=156, POS1=122, SL1=18, SL2=1 byte, SR1=11, SR2=1 byte, the four masks of the 19937 parameter set, no SIMD); the init_gen_rand / init_by_array seeding and period certification were re-implemented from the authors' reference source, which defines them; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: after init_gen_rand(1234) the first 1000 32-bit outputs of SFMT-19937 equal the 1000 values the authors published
after init_by_array({0x1234, 0x5678, 0x9abc, 0xdef0}) the first 1000 outputs equal the 1000 values the authors published

expected_values_source.what: the two blocks of 1000 32-bit outputs in the authors' SFMT.19937.out.txt (id string SFMT-19937:122-18-1-11-1:dfffffef-ddfecb7f-bffaffff-bffffff6); the seeds come from the authors' test.c
expected_values_source.note: the values are data, copied as numbers; the authors' code (SFMT.c, SFMT-common.h, test.c) was read only to confirm seeding details, parameters and the test seeds, and was not copied

negative_control: built with -DSFMT_POS1=121 (M = 121 instead of 122), 0 of 2000 published outputs match and the program exits 1 (checked on ounce-core Tier-3 and natively)
not_checked: the paper's period (2^19937-1) and equidistribution claims, and the other Mersenne exponents (607 to 216091) it tabulates; only the 19937 parameter set is run
the 64-bit output interface and the real-number conversions
the SIMD (SSE2 / AltiVec / NEON) implementations, which this plain C program does not use
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 2000 published SFMT-19937 outputs for the two seedings. It does not show the statistical claims hold.
